title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: CALVIN'S TRUCK
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Calvin, a trucker from Billings, Montana.
For twenty-six years on the road, he missed almost everything at home.
Now he's home for good. And his grown daughter Jess treats him like a stranger.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE OLD PICKUP
segments.quote: Whether you believe you can do a thing or not, you are right.
segments.author: Henry Ford
lines: In the barn sat his dad's old Ford pickup. Dead for ten years.
Calvin wanted to fix it with Jess. But he was no mechanic.
Then he saw his dad's old sign over the workbench. Henry Ford:
Whether you believe you can do a thing or not, you are right.
So he knocked on her door. Want to help me wake up Grandpa's truck?

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: JUST WATCH
segments.quote: You can observe a lot by watching.
segments.author: Yogi Berra
lines: Jess fixes brakes at a tire shop. In ten minutes, she knew that engine better than he did.
But Calvin kept giving orders. Jess got quieter.
Then he thought of Yogi Berra, the Yankees catcher:
You can observe a lot by watching.
So he handed her the wrench and just watched. That's when she started talking.
Me? I'd last about four seconds.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE BACKFIRE
segments.quote: The only man who never makes a mistake is the man who never does anything.
segments.author: Theodore Roosevelt
lines: One night, Calvin hooked up a wire wrong. The truck backfired so loud the neighbor's goats ran off.
He threw down his rag. See? I ruin everything.
Jess pointed to another of Grandpa's signs. Teddy Roosevelt:
The only man who never makes a mistake is the man who never does anything.
They fixed the wire. The goats came home Thursday.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE KEYS
segments.quote: Trust men and they will be true to you; treat them greatly and they will show themselves great.
segments.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
lines: By December, it ran. Jess asked to drive it to work in the snow.
Calvin's stomach dropped. Ice. Hills. His only kid.
Then he remembered the writer Ralph Waldo Emerson:
Trust men and they will be true to you; treat them greatly and they will show themselves great.
He tossed her the keys. She texted him when she got there. First time ever.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: NO MORE SPEECHES
segments.quote: Example is not the main thing in influencing others. It is the only thing.
segments.author: Albert Schweitzer
lines: For years, Calvin had called from the road with one speech. Finish what you start.
She never listened. But she watched him finish that truck, bolt by bolt.
Her shop's break room had a sign from Albert Schweitzer, the doctor:
Example is not the main thing in influencing others. It is the only thing.
So Calvin stopped giving speeches. He just kept showing up.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE BIG NEWS
segments.quote: Far and away the best prize that life offers is the chance to work hard at work worth doing.
segments.author: Theodore Roosevelt
lines: In spring, Jess signed up for diesel mechanic school. Big trucks. Like his.
On her brochure was Grandpa's favorite Roosevelt line:
Far and away the best prize that life offers is the chance to work hard at work worth doing.
Calvin cried a little. He says it was the diesel fumes.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Believe you can. Watch more. Try anyway. Trust. Show, don't tell. Find work worth doing.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Believe you can. Watch more. Don't fear mistakes. Trust people. Show, don't tell. Find work worth doing.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night. And call your kids. Even the grown ones.
